page: Amazon Web Services c6i.large is an entry-tier compute-optimized instance hosted on the AWS Nitro System hypervisor. It is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8375C processor running at a base clock frequency of 3.5 GHz. The instance provisions 2 vCPUs mapped to 1 physical core using two threads per core with dedicated allocation. System memory totals 4.0 GB of DDR4 operating at 3 GHz, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware instruction support includes AVX-512 extensions (AVX512F and AVX512_VNNI) alongside cryptographic accelerations such as AES, VAES, and SHA-NI. The instance includes no bundled local storage and connects with a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps without complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results highlight solid single-thread performance paired with restricted multi-thread execution capacity due to its single physical core constraint. The instance records 1881.49 on stress-ng single-core and 1622.0 on Geekbench single-core, both placing it in the average tier. Single-threaded gzip compression reaches 27.86 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression yields 10.26 GB/sec. Conversely, multi-core benchmarks show sharp throughput ceilings, evidenced by a Geekbench multi-core score of 1856.0, a PassMark CPU score of 2975.76, and an uncached memory read bandwidth of 14.26 GB/sec. Application testing demonstrates static web serving throughput of 3.16 GB/sec and Redis throughput of 1.91 million SET operations per second.

Given its small compute footprint and lack of local NVMe storage, c6i.large offers budget-conscious compute efficiency for tasks requiring modern instruction sets without heavy memory footprints. It is best deployed for lightweight web services, small API backends, build runners, microservices, and modest background utility processing.
